key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing specific wear rate by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: The combined process could improve wear-resistant nickel-based protective coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel for mechanical and power engineering components.
method: Deposit NiCrFeBSiC coatings by detonation spraying, then apply laser remelting.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Evaluate hardness, modulus, adhesion, friction, wear, and electrochemical corrosion behavior.
evidence_signal: After remelting, hardness rose from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, average friction coefficient fell from 0.535 to 0.409, and specific wear rate decreased from 2.864 × 10⁻⁴ to 1.447 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Remelting reduced coating thickness, while corrosion current density improved by only approximately 3%; application-specific thickness and corrosion requirements need validation.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
